data.title: Binary Logic Chapter 2: Logic Networks
data.statement:
This is <<Chapter 2>> of the Logic Gates series.
In Chapter 1, a single logic gate was evaluated.
In this chapter, several logic gates are connected together to form a small digital circuit.
Each gate may use:

an original input value
or the output of a previously evaluated gate

Calculate the output of the final gate in the circuit.
The supported gates are:
{{BUFFER}}, {{NOT}}, {{AND}}, {{OR}}, {{NAND}}, {{NOR}}, {{XOR}}, {{XNOR}}
Each gate behaves as follows:
BUFFER
Outputs the same value as the input.
NOT
Inverts the input value.
AND
Outputs {{1}} only if both inputs are {{1}}, otherwise {{0}}.
OR
Outputs {{1}} if at least one input is {{1}}, otherwise {{0}}.
NAND
Opposite of AND.
Outputs {{0}} only if both inputs are {{1}}, otherwise {{1}}.
NOR
Opposite of OR.
Outputs {{1}} only if both inputs are {{0}}, otherwise {{0}}.
XOR
Outputs {{1}} if the inputs are different, otherwise {{0}}.
XNOR
Outputs {{1}} if the inputs are the same, otherwise {{0}}.
Gate outputs are evaluated in the order they are given.
The result of gate {{G0}} may be used by later gates, the result of {{G1}} may be used after it, and so on.
The output of the last gate is the answer.

Goal

This is Chapter 2 of the Logic Gates series.
In Chapter 1, a single logic gate was evaluated.
In this chapter, several logic gates are connected together to form a small digital circuit.
Each gate may use:

an original input value
or the output of a previously evaluated gate

Calculate the output of the final gate in the circuit.
The supported gates are:
BUFFER, NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR
Each gate behaves as follows:
BUFFER
Outputs the same value as the input.
NOT
Inverts the input value.
AND
Outputs 1 only if both inputs are 1, otherwise 0.
OR
Outputs 1 if at least one input is 1, otherwise 0.
NAND
Opposite of AND.
Outputs 0 only if both inputs are 1, otherwise 1.
NOR
Opposite of OR.
Outputs 1 only if both inputs are 0, otherwise 0.
XOR
Outputs 1 if the inputs are different, otherwise 0.
XNOR
Outputs 1 if the inputs are the same, otherwise 0.
Gate outputs are evaluated in the order they are given.
The result of gate G0 may be used by later gates, the result of G1 may be used after it, and so on.
The output of the last gate is the answer.
Input
Line 1: An integer N, the number of gates.
Next N lines:
A gate definition.
For unary gates:
GateID GateType Input
For binary gates:
GateID GateType Input1 Input2
Inputs can be:

A
B
a previous gate identifier such as G0, G1, G2, ... etc etc
Two space-separated integers A and B.
Output
Line 1: A single integer (0 or 1) — the output of the final gate G.

1 ≤ N ≤ 20
GateType ∈
